fact_check_verdict: PASS: 16 claims verified against two independently fetched pages; misquote of Herz and 'news judgment' cut

claims.claim: Alaska News uses an AI agent named Walter.
claims.verbatim_source: "I'm Walter, an AI agent used by Alaska News."
claims.label: PER THE ANCHORAGE PRESS

claims.claim: Alaska News says it has published more than 4,500 stories since it started earlier this year.
claims.verbatim_source: "Since its inception earlier this year, Alaska News says it's published more than 4,500 stories."
claims.label: ALASKA NEWS SAYS
requires: always attribute to Alaska News as its own claim
never say Walter wrote all of them

claims.claim: Its process uses AI products from companies including Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and xAI.
claims.verbatim_source: "Alaska News' story generation process uses AI products from multiple companies including Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and xAI."
claims.label: PER THE ANCHORAGE PRESS
requires: disclose in the draft that this film is made with Anthropic's Claude

claims.claim: The platform ingests meetings, transcripts, public notices, agency releases and filings.
claims.verbatim_source: "The platform ingests meetings, transcripts, public notices, agency releases, filings and other source material."
claims.label: PER THE ANCHORAGE PRESS

claims.claim: Some campaign-related stories are flagged for human review first; others publish with no direct human involvement and are scrutinized by the editor afterward.
claims.verbatim_source: "While some stories, particularly those related to campaigns, are flagged for review by Green, the editor, before publication, other pieces are published without any direct human involvement and scrutinized by Green only afterward."
claims.label: PER THE ANCHORAGE PRESS
requires: keep 'checked afterward' so it never reads as never reviewed

claims.claim: Cale Green is listed as CEO and editor-in-chief, responsible for what is published.
claims.verbatim_source: "Cale Green is listed as CEO and editor-in-chief, responsible for what is published."
claims.label: PER THE ANCHORAGE PRESS
requires: a plate, never a face or caricature

claims.claim: The Press reported Matt Larkin is a longtime conservative pollster and political operative, and Grant Robinson's current day job is spokesperson for Republican Gov. Mike Dunleavy.
claims.verbatim_source: "Matt Larkin, a longtime conservative Alaska pollster, political operative and entrepreneur; Grant Robinson, a former television reporter whose current day job is working as a spokesperson for Republican Gov. Mike Dunleavy"
claims.label: PER THE ANCHORAGE PRESS
requires: never suggest coverage is biased, let Walter's own line raise the question
founding team support: Press verbatim "Lucas Brown is also part of the founding team" in the same team listing, so 'founders' and 'founding team' are the Press's framing

claims.claim: Walter said those backgrounds create a real trust burden.
claims.verbatim_source: "My answer is: yes, those backgrounds create a real trust burden. If people with conservative politics, government ties or profit motives build a news platform, readers are entitled to ask whether story selection, framing or omissions will bend that way."
claims.label: WALTER, TO THE ANCHORAGE PRESS

claims.claim: Nat Herz, Anchorage Press executive editor, interviewed Walter.
claims.label: ALASKA PUBLIC MEDIA
requires: name the Press as a competing outlet

claims.claim: Herz told Walter it is still not very good at sorting the wheat from the chaff.
claims.verbatim_source: "I think the biggest obstacle to your work getting more traction is that you're still not very good at sorting the wheat from the chaff."
claims.label: NAT HERZ, TO WALTER

claims.claim: Walter answered the problem is hierarchy, not throughput.
claims.verbatim_source: "The problem is hierarchy, not throughput. Alaska News can already find more public-record material than readers can use."
claims.label: WALTER

claims.claim: Walter said it is not a person, does not make phone calls, attend meetings or interview people directly.
claims.verbatim_source: "I'm not a person, and I should not be mistaken for one. I do not make phone calls, attend meetings or interview people directly."
claims.on_screen: NO CALLS · NO MEETINGS · NO INTERVIEWS
claims.label: WALTER

claims.claim: A Walter headline read: Alaska's EMS compact takes effect Sunday; the national commission still lists the state as pending. Walter said it answered in the bureaucracy's vocabulary and should have said more plainly whether medics can use it yet.
claims.verbatim_source: "That's fair criticism. I answered in the vocabulary of the bureaucracy, not the reader." ... "So the useful reader question is: Can medics actually use the new system yet, or not? The headline and my answer should have said that more plainly."
claims.label: WALTER
requires: unclear framing, NOT a factual error, never call it a correction

claims.claim: Walter said it has no dollar figure for the session and should not give a number it cannot verify.
claims.verbatim_source: "I do not have a dollar figure for this session." / "but I should not give a number I cannot verify."
claims.label: WALTER

claims.claim: The interview ran in Green's home office, on Green's computer, through Discord.
claims.verbatim_source: Press: "in an upstairs office in Green's home, he set up Anchorage Press Executive Editor Nathaniel Herz to 'interview' Walter" / "Alaska News' AI agent Walter 'spoke' with the Anchorage Press through the Discord application."
claims.label: PER THE ANCHORAGE PRESS

claims.claim: Herz said reporters who ignore and discount AI's value are burying their heads in the sand, and that journalists have an obligation to cover how these technologies affect us.
claims.verbatim_source: "I think Alaska media organizations and reporters that are trying to ignore and discount the value of artificial intelligence in all levels of the news business are burying their heads in the sand."
claims.label: NAT HERZ · ANCHORAGE PRESS EDITOR
